THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL, J. DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 COMMON JUDGMENT

These appeals are filed by the claimants/appellants being aggrieved by the common Judgment and award dated 08.09.2014 passed in MVC No.1097/2012 and in MVC No.1347/2012 by the Fast Track Court II and Additional MACT, Belagavi, wherein, the petition of the claimants/appellants filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 were dismissed.

2. Brief facts giving rise for filing of these appeals are that, on 30.03.2012 on Chitturu Bangarapalam road, at Madhavnagar Bridge, a road accident took place between the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-07/F- 1469 and a car bearing registration No.KA-22/P-4410 which was moving towards opposite direction.

In the said accident Sri. Chandrakant Vithappa Dattawad, daughter- in-law of the petitioner No.1, sister-in-law of the petitioner Nos.2 to 4 and brother-in-law of the petitioner Nos.5 to 6 in MVC No.1347/2012 and Sri. Uday Nadagouda in MVC No.1397/2012 have died, who were traveling in the said car.
The owner of the said Maruti Car also died in the said accident.
The above referred claimants have approached the MACT Belagavi praying for compensation.

The MACT, Belagavi vide common Judgment and award dated 08.09.2014 dismissed Siddawwa W/O Vithappa Dattawade vs The Divisional Manager on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76153336/

sentences.text: 4 the claim petitions.
In the aforesaid factual matrix the present appeals have been filed and they were heard together.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants Sri. Srinivas Nadamani, appearing on behalf of Sri.
S.B.Hebballi, submits that, the tribunal has dismissed the claim petition without appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record in its proper perspective.

It is submitted that, the finding recorded by the tribunal that due to the rash and negligent driving of the car the said accident has occurred is contrary to evidence on record and the driver of the KSRTC bus has also contributed for the accident.
These aspects have not been properly appreciated by the tribunal which has resulted in dismissal of the claim petitions.
It is also submitted that, the tribunal has failed to take note of the fact that, owner of the car has died in the said accident and his legal representatives are the claimants before the tribunal.

Hence, the dismissal of the claim petition by the tribunal on the ground of non-joinder of necessary party is bad in law and required to be interfered in the present appeal by awarding just and fair compensation.

4. Per contra, Sri. M.K.Soudagar, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 and Sri.
S.C.Bhuti, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supports the impugned Judgment and award passed by the MACT, Belagavi and submits that, the MACT has given a categorical finding that due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by the driver of the car the said accident has happened and in the said accident the owner of the car has also succumbed to the injuries.
It is further submitted that, the jurisdictional police after investigation have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the car for rash and negligent driving and causing the said accident.

It is also submitted that, the tribunal has considered the material on record and on appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence has given categorical finding that due to rash and negligent driving of the car the accident has taken place and the claimants have not arrayed the owner/legal representative of the owner as respondents in the claim petitions, the said finding of the tribunal does not suffer from any illegality calling for interference in the present appeal.
5. We have heard the learned counsels for the parties and perused the material on record.

6. It is not in dispute that, on 30.03.2012 at 11.30 p.m., on Chittur, Bangarapalum Road, at Mahadev Nagar Bridge a road accident took place between the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-07/F-1469 and a Maruti car bearing registration No.KA-22/P-4410 and in the said accident Sri. Chandrakant Dattawade and Sri. Uday Nadagouda along with others have died.
It is also not in dispute that, the legal representatives of the deceased have approached the MACT, Belagavi by filing the claim petition for seeking compensation under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1988.
On meticulous appreciation of oral and documentary evidence on record, it is evident that P.W.1 and P.W.2 have deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the bus, the said accident took place.

However,
R.W.1 and R.W.2 who has supported the case of respondents stating that, the accident has caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Maruti Car.
On perusal of the investigation material which clearly shows that, due to rash and negligent driving of the Maturi car driven by its driver, the accident took place.

It is also admitted that, the investigation officer has filed charge- sheet against the driver of the car for causing the accident, which clearly establishes the fact that, the accident was caused by the driver of the Maruti car.

On perusal of the Exhibits P.1 to P.23 and Siddawwa W/O Vithappa Dattawade vs The Divisional Manager on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76153336/
5 Exhibit R.7, the copies of FIR, Complaint, Panchanama, M.V.I. Report, Sketch, and four photographs, it is evident that the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the Maruti car by its driver.

sentences.text:
On bear perusal of the sketch at Ex.P.10 and on appreciation of testimony of R.W.2,
which corroborates with the said sketch, it is very much clear that, the bus was coming from extremely left side of the road, however, the Maruti car crossing the middle of the road and came extremely right side of the road and dashed the offending bus.
These evidences clearly establishes the fact that, the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the Maruti car.

7. The tribunal has recorded the finding that, the claimants have not arrayed the owner as a party to the - 10 - proceedings and only they have arrayed the Insurance company as a respondent to their claim petition, the first respondent being the Insurer of the car bearing registration No.KA-22/P-4410 is not liable to pay any compensation to the claimant and further the deceased in MVC No.1397/2012 namely Uday Nadagouda was the owner and the deceased Chandrakant Dattawade was the driver of the said car bearing registration No.KA-22/P- 4410 and the said driver of the car steps in to the shoes of the owner of the car.

Hence, they are not entitle for the compensation from the first respondent-Insurance company since both the deceased are not considered as third parties to the contract of Insurance between the owner and the Insurer of the said car.
The aforesaid finding do not suffer from any perversity and they are based on settle principle of law, we do not find any error in the said finding calling for interference in the present appeals.

The tribunal on meticulous appreciation of evidence on record has given the finding that due to rash and negligent driving of the Maruti car the said accident has took place and rightly rejected the claim petitions.
We do not find any reason to interfere with the said findings.
In the result, the appeals are dismissed.
No order as to costs.
